Binance Blockchain Week Bangkok 2026: First Speakers Announced

2026-11-11

Main Takeaways

  • The first wave of speakers for Binance Blockchain Week Bangkok 2026 is confirmed, including Arthur Hayes, and CZ, alongside policymakers and institutional leaders.

  • Under the theme Evolve, the event explores how traditional finance and digital assets are converging, from payments and tokenized stocks to real-world assets and AI.

  • Join us at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center in Bangkok on November 28–29, 2026. Tickets on sale now, with further speaker and agenda updates to follow.

Binance Blockchain Week returns to Asia this November, and the speaker lineup for Bangkok is here. This year’s theme, Evolve, reflects a shift already under way: traditional finance and digital assets are merging into one connected system, from payments and tokenized stocks to real-world assets, while barriers to entry keep falling.

On November 28–29, policymakers, institutional leaders, and crypto builders take the stage at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center for two days of keynotes, expert-led panels, and hands-on workshops. Here’s who’s confirmed so far, how to join the build-up, and how to get your ticket.

Who’s Speaking at Binance Blockchain Week Bangkok 2026

The first wave of speakers brings together policymakers, central bankers, institutional asset managers, and technology leaders. Policy is front and center, with Gizzat Baitursynov, Vice Minister of AI and Digital Development in Kazakhstan, and Shaun Tan of Gelephu Mindfulness City in Bhutan bringing the view from inside governments.

“Regulatory innovation is no longer confined to traditional financial centers. Increasingly, emerging jurisdictions are shaping the future of digital finance. The regulatory frameworks and financial infrastructure countries build today will determine where capital flows, where companies choose to grow, and which markets lead tomorrow,” said Richard Teng, Co-CEO of Binance.

On the market side, Arthur Hayes, CIO of Maelstrom, is joined by CZ, founder of Giggle Academy and, of course, Binance.

As traditional finance and digital assets converge, the lineup follows the money on-chain, with leaders from BlackRock, Franklin Templeton, Visa, and PayPay joining alongside voices from crypto media and research, and Binance leadership including Co-CEOs Richard Teng and Yi He.

The Speaker Lineup

Policymakers and Regulators

  • Gizzat Baitursynov | Vice Minister, Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development of the Republic of Kazakhstan

  • Shaun Tan | Head of Crypto and Fintech Growth, Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC), Bhutan

Industry Leaders

  • Arthur Hayes | CIO, Maelstrom

  • CZ | Founder, Giggle Academy and Binance

  • Matthew Roszak | Chairman, Bloq 

Institutions, Payments, and Technology

  • Athena Y | CEO, United Stables

  • Dan Maley | APAC Head of Digital Assets, BlackRock

  • Ella Zhang | Managing Partner & Head of YZi Labs

  • Kelly Sohn | Head of Digital Asset, Mirae Asset Securities (HK) Limited

  • Min Linn | Managing Director, Head of Global Business Development, Ondo Finance

  • Nischint Sanghavi | Head of Digital Currencies, Asia Pacific, Visa

  • Roger Bayston | Head of Digital Assets Ecosystem Development, Franklin Templeton

  • Sushant Singh | APAC Expansion, Tether

  • Thomas Chen | Chief Business Officer, BNB Chain

  • Yoshi Yokokawa | Co-Founder and CEO, Alpaca

  • Yuki Jinguji | Head of Financial Business Development, PayPay Corporation

Media, Research, and Data

  • Alex Svanevik | CEO, Nansen

  • Anastasia Melachrinos | Head of Research, Kaiko

  • Joshua de Vos | Research Lead, CoinDesk

  • Nic Puckrin | Founder, Coin Bureau

  • Roosa Kivisto | Head of Business Development, DeFiLlama

Binance Leadership

  • Antonio Alvarez Lorenzo | Deputy Chief Compliance Officer, Binance

  • Catherine Chen | Head of VIP and Institutional, Binance

  • Eowyn Chen | Chief Marketing Officer, Binance

  • Jeff Li | VP of Product, Binance

  • Nirun Fuwattananukul | CEO, Binance TH by Gulf Binance

  • Richard Teng | Co-CEO, Binance

  • SB Seker | Head of APAC, Binance

  • Shunyet Jan | Head of Exchange and Trading, Binance

  • Thomas Gregory | VP of Payments and Fiat, Binance

  • Yi He | Co-CEO and Co-Founder, Binance

More speakers will be announced in the coming weeks.

Join the Road to Binance Blockchain Week on Binance Square

You don’t have to wait until Bangkok to be part of the conversation. On November 17 at 15:00 UTC+4, Binance is hosting a special pre-event Binance livestream session on Binance Square, giving the community an early look at the themes behind this year’s event, Evolve.

Exclusive guests will join the session, and there’s a $5,000 red packet giveaway on offer. Whether you’re heading to Bangkok or following from anywhere in the world, it’s a chance to get up to speed on what’s coming before the speakers take the stage on November 28–29.

Final Thoughts

Finance is opening up, and there’s never been a better time to be part of the conversation. This year’s program follows three shifts: traditional and digital markets converging on shared infrastructure, AI reshaping how people manage capital, and governments, institutions, and builders working together on clear, trusted frameworks. The first speakers confirmed for Bangkok span all three.

“As traditional finance and digital assets converge, our focus remains constant: improving access, strengthening user protections, and delivering seamless experiences,” said Yi He, Co-CEO and Co-Founder of Binance. “Binance Blockchain Week convenes the architects of this transformation.” Tune in to the Binance Square livestream on November 17 for an early look, then join us in Bangkok on November 28–29.

Event: Binance Blockchain Week Bangkok 2026, Asia Edition

Dates: November 28–29, 2026

Venue: Queen Sirikit National Convention Center, Bangkok, Thailand

→ Get your ticket at www.binanceblockchainweek.com and join us in Bangkok this November.

Tokenized Equities Reach a Record AUM of $4.8B as bStocks Becomes the Largest Issuer

2026-11-10

Main Takeaways

  • Tokenized equities AUM has reached an all-time high of $4.8B, growing 164% between June and early November, according to Binance Research.

  • bStocks passed $1.5B in AUM in 145 days, making it the largest tokenized equities issuer by AUM. 

  • Adoption spans generations and regions. Gen Z makes up 46% of bStocks users, Millennials account for 78% of trading value, and emerging and frontier markets generate about 70% of volume.

The tokenized equities market sits at an all-time high of $4.8B in assets under management (AUM). Within that market, bStocks is the largest issuer by AUM, having surpassed $1.5B. The sections below look at how the market reached this point, who is using bStocks, and how users can check what backs each token.

A Brief History of Tokenized Equities

Today’s tokenized equities build on years of groundwork, from early pilots to a regulated market traded by millions of users worldwide.

2019-2021: Proof of Concept

The first wave of tokenized assets was proof-of-concept work. Franklin Templeton launched FOBXX, also known by its digital token BENJI. It was the first U.S.-registered mutual fund to record share ownership on a public blockchain. During the same period, Singapore's largest bank, DBS, settled its first S$15 million digital bond on its own regulated exchange.

2022-2024: Real-World Assets (RWA)

The second wave shifted toward yield-bearing real-world assets, led by tokenized U.S. Treasuries. Where FOBXX was a public fund open to retail investors, BlackRock brought its USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund (BUIDL) onto blockchain networks as a private fund for qualified institutions. This made it one of the first institutional private funds to natively integrate into DeFi.

2025-2026: Mainstream Integration

The current wave has brought mainstream integration and more legal clarity. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission issued a temporary five-year conditional exemption for tokenized securities venues, while South Korea’s official tokenized securities framework is set to take effect on February 4, 2027. 

Why Did Binance Integrate bStocks?

Our core product philosophy hasn’t changed since our founding as a digital asset exchange: we have always believed in expanding financial access worldwide. By giving users 1:1 exposure to stocks and ETFs through crypto technology, bStocks opens new pathways into traditional finance. 

Crypto-native users can diversify their exposure in a familiar format without needing a separate brokerage account, while traditional stock investors get a parallel market that stays open when Wall Street goes dark.

Who is Trading bStocks?

Data from Binance Research shows a diverse user base: roughly 56% of bStocks trading volume takes place outside regular U.S. market hours. Gen Z makes up 46% of users and trades more of its volume on weekends than any other group. Millennials hold positions the longest and account for 78% of trading value.

Users in emerging and frontier markets have generated roughly 70% of bStocks volume since launch. Many of them live in regions where U.S.-listed equities have historically been hard to access.

Are bStocks Backed 1:1?

Each token is backed 1:1 by real shares and ETFs held by a regulated custodian. Reserves are reconciled and published daily on our Proof of Collateral page, so holders can confirm their tokens are fully backed.

Final Thoughts

Tokenized equities are still a tiny fraction of traditional equities. In a market this young, our ranking  – while a welcome milestone – matters less than the direction of the entire category, which grew 81% between June and early November outside of bStocks.

We believe the way people hold and trade traditional assets may change significantly in the coming years, and we’ll continue to build and expand our bStocks offering and TradFi product suite with this, and our users, in mind.

A Status You Can Wear: New Year Gifts for Binance VIPs

2026-11-10

Main Takeaways

  • Binance is thanking its VIP community with the New Year VIP Campaign, a limited-time gift program for eligible users.

  • Hold VIP 1 or higher for 30 consecutive days, from 2026-11-16 to 2026-12-16, and the lowest tier you hold during that period decides your gift.

  • VIP 1–2 can earn the VIP Aviator Set (bomber jacket and cap), and VIP 3–9 the VIP Alpine Set (ski jacket and goggles).

The turn of the year is a natural moment to take stock of what you’ve built, what you’ve learned, and what you’re aiming for next. To mark the start of 2027, Binance is launching the New Year VIP Campaign — a limited-time, tier-based gift program for eligible VIP users.

We’re saying thanks with something you can actually wear: a Binance-branded bomber jacket and cap, or ski jacket and goggles, depending on the tier you maintain throughout the campaign period. Read on for how the tiers work, what’s in each set, how to get yours, and what else comes with VIP.

Campaign Period: 2026-11-16 00:00 (UTC) to 2026-12-16 00:00 (UTC). Please note: this campaign is not available in all regions. See the full terms and conditions here.

Check Your VIP Status

How It Works

Staying power is what counts here. Your gift depends on the Binance VIP level you maintain during the Campaign Period. To take part, you need to be VIP 1 or higher on 2026-11-16 00:00 (UTC), then keep your VIP status for 30 consecutive days through 2026-12-16 00:00 (UTC). Every day in between counts: the lowest tier you hold during those 30 days decides your gift, and dropping to Regular User at any point during the Campaign Period means no gift. The table below shows which set goes with which tier.

Eligibility and Rewards

Maintained VIP Level*

Reward

VIP 1–2

VIP Aviator Set

(Binance-branded bomber jacket and cap)

VIP 3–9

VIP Alpine Set

(Binance-branded ski jacket and goggles)

Please Note: 

  • Your Binance VIP level is updated daily at 00:00 (UTC) and reflects your activity from the previous day. To make sure your VIP status counts from the start of the Campaign Period on 2026-11-16, you must meet the required criteria by 23:59 (UTC) on 2026-11-15.

  • *A user’s Maintained VIP Level will be determined based on the lowest VIP level maintained during the 30 consecutive days of the Campaign Period. 

    • For example, if you’re VIP 3 for 20 days and VIP 2 for 10 days during the Campaign Period, your maintained VIP level counts as VIP 2, and you’d be eligible for the VIP Aviator Set (for VIP 1-2). 

    • To qualify for the VIP Alpine Set (for VIP 3-9), you need to maintain VIP 3 or higher throughout the entire 30-day period.

  • If you’re downgraded to Regular User status at any point during the Campaign Period, you won’t be eligible for any reward.

  • VIP level upgrades granted via voucher or manual adjustment are not eligible. 

  • Users covered by the protected tier under the VIP Level Protection Program during the period from 2026-11-03 to 2026-12-02 remain eligible.

  • Important note: VIP rewards are only available to users in eligible jurisdictions. Availability of the merchandise may vary depending on your country or region. Certain items may not be available in your jurisdiction. Where an item is unavailable, Binance may offer an alternative item of similar value at its discretion.

  • The Terms and Conditions for Prize Promotions apply. 

What’s in Each Set and How to Get Yours

There are two sets, and the tier you maintain through the Campaign Period decides which one comes your way. Each eligible user can receive one gift, and you’ll share your size along with your shipping address. Here’s what’s inside each set, and how to get your details in.

Gift details

  • VIP Aviator Set: Includes a Binance-branded bomber jacket and cap. Available to eligible users who maintain VIP 1–2 for 30 consecutive days during the Campaign Period.

  • VIP Alpine Set: Includes a Binance-branded ski jacket and goggles. Available to eligible users who maintain VIP 3 or higher for 30 consecutive days during the Campaign Period.

Address collection

  • Reward distribution and winner information will be released by 2026-12-30.

  • All eligible users can submit their shipping address and sizing information via the My VIP > Explore > My Gifts page. 

What Else Comes with Binance VIP

The gifts are a seasonal thank-you, but VIP is built to be useful all year round. It also comes with lower trading fees, higher Earn rates, tools for managing larger portfolios, and access to events and a dedicated point of contact. 

Here’s the rundown, with some benefits varying by tier.

  • Trading Fees: Lower Spot and Futures rates, with discounts increasing at every VIP tier

29 October 2026 Binance Security Incident: Initial Findings and Response Update

2026-11-03

On 29 October 2026, Binance experienced a serious and highly sophisticated security incident. This should not have happened, and we apologise for the concern, disruption and uncertainty it caused our users, partners and the wider industry.

Our first responsibility is to protect users. Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users. We have already set aside more than 100% of the funds required to cover the loss. As of 31 October 2026, 98% of the impacted token assets have been replenished and are verifiable on our Proof of Reserves page. We are in the process of purchasing the outstanding, more illiquid assets.

Approximately USD 6.34 billion in digital assets were impacted by the incident. As of this update, approximately USD 2.85 billion in digital assets have been frozen or intercepted, subject to reconciliation and market price volatility.

We have taken immediate action to contain the incident and strengthen the systems involved. The entry points identified as having been used in the attack have been closed. Systems touched in the attack path have been rebuilt or replaced. We have also implemented tighter device controls, enhanced wallet-service risk controls and expanded AI-based behavioural anomaly detection.

This is our initial report. It covers what we know today and what we have already improved. The investigation remains ongoing and our findings will be subject to further independent review. Some technical details will remain confidential to prevent malicious actors from using them to plan attacks. We are engaging independent security firms for further review. 

The latest information released by the Federal Bureau of Investigation indicates that the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea is responsible for this incident.

We are sharing this initial report because security improves when the industry learns together.

What happened on 29 October

The attack unfolded quickly across several networks.

The attacker exploited unauthorized access to an internal wallet signing service to initiate transactions outside the normal withdrawal process.

Between 20:05 UTC and 20:09 UTC, five Binance hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker-controlled address.

Binance hot wallets on Solana and Optimism sent approximately 970,500 SOL and 44.2 million OP to attacker-controlled addresses.

Binance then received an internal alert regarding large-volume transfers and immediately began investigating.

Binance hot wallet sent 18,270 BTC to an attacker-controlled address. 

The attacker then used the signing service to exploit Ethereum’s EIP-7702 authorization mechanism. EIP-7702 allows an account to delegate certain execution rights to a smart contract without exposing the private key. In this case, the attacker used that mechanism to give an attacker-controlled smart contract partial execution rights over a Binance hot wallet. 

Binance immediately initiated multiple containment measures, including suspending withdrawals to restrict further outflows, coordinating with partners to freeze affected tokens, and taking steps to revoke unauthorized permissions. These efforts froze a total of $2.85 billion in assets.

However, suspending withdrawals alone could not stop all unauthorized asset movements. The malicious EIP-7702 authorizations existed on-chain and operated independently of Binance’s normal withdrawal infrastructure.The attackers submitted 50 signing transactions to manipulate the account nonce and establish malicious delegation authorizations. Once established, these authorizations enabled the attackers to continue moving assets independently of Binance's normal withdrawal infrastructure. Binance needed additional transactions to revoke these on-chain authorizations.

The containment process involved additional technical complexities. Because the hot wallet used Multi-Party Computation (MPC), there was no single private key that could be used to immediately revoke the malicious EIP-7702 authorizations. The team therefore developed and executed a specialized procedure to revoke these authorizations, which required additional time. Furthermore, suspending withdrawals and shutting down hot wallet services did not automatically invalidate existing on-chain authorizations.

These challenges extended the time required to fully contain the unauthorized asset movements. We are reviewing the incident response process, signing policy coverage, hot wallet controls and identifying opportunities to further strengthen our ability to respond rapidly to threats in the future.

The final unauthorized transfer of 2,961.9 ETH finalised on-chain at 23:56 UTC. The transaction had previously been broadcast and remained pending before subsequently finalising. No further unauthorised transfers were observed after.

At 00:10 UTC on 30 October 2026, Binance executed a new authorization from the Binance14 hot wallet to the zero address, clearing the EIP-7702 delegation code.

Attack Preparation 

Our current investigation indicates that this was a sophisticated, multi-stage campaign. It was not a single isolated breach or a simple phishing incident. The attackers combined a range of techniques, including social engineering by fake recruitment interviews, malicious software downloads, compromised internal AI tooling, endpoint compromise, and an advanced transaction-authorisation method.

  • June 2026 — Supply chain attack. Engineer A from Wallet DevOps downloaded a tampered Homebrew installation in order to install a popular AI coding tool after searching for it on a search engine. Our security team detected the anomaly, replaced the device, and rotated all related credentials as a proactive security action. However, Engineer A’s role and his related colleagues on our wallet infrastructure team was exposed to the hacker. 

  • Throughout 2026, Binance's security team detected and prevented 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threat cases. These attempts reflect the persistent threat posed by state-sponsored actors targeting the cryptocurrency industry. The techniques include fraudulent job interviews, malicious software disguised as popular developer tools, compromised software packages and browser extensions, fake video conferencing applications, and social engineering campaigns designed to steal credentials or deploy remote access malware.

  • September 2026 — social engineering. Software Engineer B was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform by an individual posing as a Project Director. Software Engineer B had a profile on the platform that referenced his experience at Binance. The purported Project Director arranged a first-round interview with a HR representative, followed by a second-round interview with an individual claiming to be the CEO of a fictitious company.

    • In the first round, the purported HR representative conducted a live video interview with Software Engineer B. The interviewer shared a social media account with him, including personal photos and videos posted on the platform, in order to build trust. This was more advanced and deceptive than previously seen social engineering approaches. 

    • The second interview was conducted in a popular social chat app, near the end of the interview, Engineer B was instructed to download an “assignment” containing a malicious code repository onto his work computer. The repository contained malicious code that executed during the setup process, initiating a series of unauthorized activities.

    • The malware employed sophisticated obfuscation and evasion techniques, including replacing a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version to execute commands and establish communication with an attacker-controlled external server. The 0-day malware was not detected by the endpoint security protection tools at the time. The attacker also took steps to conceal the malicious activity and remove traces of the compromise, making detection and subsequent investigation more challenging.

    • The script executed the below steps by applying obfuscation techniques to evade security detection.

CREATE  /opt/homebrew/Cellar/pyenv/2.8.0/libexec/pyenv_  

MODIFY  pyenv_ → 3,414 B  

DELETE  .../libexec/pyenv  (3,344 B)      ← remove the valid pyenv

RENAME  pyenv_ → pyenv  (3,414 B)  ← replace it with a malicious version

DELETE  /opt/homebrew/bin/pyenv  (3,414 B)

ln  (create a new symlink)  +  spawn zsh

  • 20 October, 2026 — use of an internal AI tool as a springboard. The attacker leveraged the compromised computer of engineer B and used an internal AI tool to gain control over the Wallet DevOps Engineer A and another Wallet Software Engineer C. The attacker soon discovered Wallet DevOps Engineer A had a container deployment permission token on his computer.

  • 29 October, 2026 — reach into wallet signing operations. On 29 October between 17:15 and 19:56, the attacker logged onto Software Engineer C’s computer, used the credentials stolen from Wallet DevOps Engineer A, deployed a container, and triggered a malicious script to launch the attack.

What we have done

As of Nov 3, 2026, we have taken the following actions:

  • Rebuilt the affected wallet system in a new environment.

  • Rebuilt the affected internal AI tool and access controls.

  • Replaced affected devices.

  • Decommissioned credentials and tokens related to affected engineers.

  • Completed enhanced security scans across all employee devices.

  • Enhanced AI-based behavioural anomaly detection.

  • Strengthened wallet-service risk controls.

  • Worked with law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze affected assets.

We will continue to strengthen our measures as the investigation progresses. There are a number of security measures we have implemented and are implementing that will remain private to prevent malicious actors from compromising our security.

Further actions

We are taking the following steps immediately.

1. Independent cybersecurity review

We are engaging independent third-party cybersecurity experts to conduct a comprehensive review of the incident, validate our findings and recommend additional measures. The scope and findings of that review will inform our continuing remediation work.

2. Expanded investment in AI security and prevention

We are increasing investment in AI-enabled detection, endpoint protection, developer-environment security and behavioural anomaly monitoring.

3. Security research fund and industry initiatives

We are working on establishing a security research fund and targeted initiatives with leading AI companies, industry participants and security firms focused on AI security in blockchain environments.

We will continue to proactively share information as and when we have it.

Covered Call and Cash-Secured Put Are Now Live on Binance Stock Options

2026-10-27

Main Takeaways

  • Covered Call lets you receive an option premium in exchange for accepting an obligation to sell shares you already hold at the strike price. 

  • Cash-Secured Put lets you receive an option premium in exchange for accepting an obligation to buy shares at the strike price.

  • Both strategies trade from the same Binance account and Funding Wallet you already use for Stock Options, with physical settlement in real shares.

On September 1, 2026, we launched our flagship Stock Options product, paving the way for millions of users to buy calls or puts on over 1,000 U.S.-listed stocks and ETFs with physical settlement. Today, we’re opening the other side of the trade, which is something many of our Options traders have been asking for. 

Covered Call and Cash-Secured Put let you sell (write) options contracts, collecting a premium upfront while your shares or USDC stay set aside as collateral until the position closes, expires, or is assigned. Below, we walk through how each strategy works, an example of each, and how to place your first order.

Covered Calls: Earn Premium on Shares You Already Hold

If you hold shares and don’t expect the price to rise much past where you’d be happy selling, a Covered Call lets those shares earn income from premium payments.

  1. You sell a call option backed by the required number of underlying shares.

  2. You receive the option premium when the order is filled, less applicable fees.

  3. If the option expires without assignment, you keep the shares and the premium.

  4. If the option is assigned, you must sell the shares at the strike price, even if their market price is higher.

Here’s what that looks like in practice. Let’s say you own a stock at $100. You sell a call option with a $110 strike price and collect a $3 premium. 

If the stock stays below $110, the option expires worthless and you keep both the shares and the $3 premium. If the stock rises to $110 or above, the buyer exercises the option and your shares are sold at $110. 

That $110 is the most you can get – along with the $3 premium – no matter how high the stock actually goes. If it goes up to $150, you still only sell at $110 and miss the extra $40. 

In short, you’re trading away unlimited upside for guaranteed income, especially if you’re not expecting the stock to rally much past $110 anyway.

Cash-Secured Put: Earn Premium While You Wait for Your Entry Price

A Cash-Secured Put suits a stock you would be happy to own at a lower price. It lets you collect premium income while you wait for the stock to reach that price, rather than placing a limit order and waiting with nothing to show for it either way.

  1. You sell a put option and provide enough USDC to meet the full purchase obligation. 

  2. You receive the option premium when the order is filled, less applicable fees.

  3. If the option expires without assignment, the collateral is released and you keep the premium.

  4. If the option is assigned, you buy the required shares at the strike price.

Here’s what that looks like in practice. Let’s say a stock trades at $100 and you want to buy it at $90. You sell a put option with a $90 strike price and collect a $3 premium.

If the stock stays above $90, the option expires worthless, you keep the $3 premium, and you never buy. If it drops to $90 or below, you’re obligated to buy at $90, no matter how far the price has fallen. The $3 premium brings your effective cost down to $87 a share.

This works out well if the stock settles close to $90. But the premium is a fixed $3 cushion, not a safety net: if the stock crashes to $70, that $3 barely dents the $17-a-share gap between what you paid and what it’s now worth.

In short, you’re getting paid to wait for the price you wanted: if the stock is still at or below $90 when the option expires, you end up buying at the same price a limit order would have gotten you, plus the $3 premium on top.

How to Place Your First Covered Call or Cash-Secured Put

  1. Enable options access. Make sure your account is enabled for Stock Options. If not, complete the Options Suitability Quiz and sign the disclaimer.

  2. Prepare your collateral. For a Covered Call, hold the underlying shares; for a Cash-Secured Put, hold enough USDC in your Funding Wallet.

  3. Open Options. Go to the stock’s k-line page and select the [Options] tab, then pick an expiration date and strike price from the options chain.

  4. Switch to Sell. Toggle the order form to [Sell]. Max Sell shows the largest number of contracts you can sell based on your shares or USDC, and the Collateral field shows what will be frozen.

  5. Confirm and place order. Tap [Preview]. If this is your first time, a Covered Call or Cash-Secured Put Risk Notice will appear. Make sure to read it carefully before placing your order.

Final Thoughts

Covered Call and Cash-Secured Put extend Stock Options from a long-only product into one where you can also generate income and target your entry prices. Instead of just holding and sitting still, you can now put your shares or your USDC to work, whether that means earning on positions you already hold or getting paid until the price you want comes along.

It’s another step forward in our vision of having all finance on Binance. It all runs through the same account and Funding Wallet you already use, giving you more ways to express a view on stocks, not just buy and hold them.

Binance Intelligence Explained: Binance AI vs. Binance AI Pro vs. Agent OS

2026-10-26

Main Takeaways

  • Binance Intelligence is a lineup of three AI products: Binance AI, an in-app personal assistant for everyday users; Binance AI Pro, a no-code financial agent that turns trading ideas into automated workflows; and Agent OS, a developer platform for connecting external AI agents to Binance’s tools and deep liquidity.

  • What separates them is their main capabilities. Binance AI only ever informs and doesn’t act, AI Pro helps users build automated strategies without code, and Agent OS hands execution to an external agent that a developer connects and grants permissions to.

  • All three products keep the user in charge by design. Permissions, funding limits, isolated sub-accounts, and the ability to revoke access at any time run through every product.

Under the banner of Binance Intelligence, Binance has launched three different AI products in the past few months: Binance AI, Binance AI Pro, and Agent OS. If you’ve found yourself wondering what separates them, or which one actually fits what you’re trying to do, you’re not alone. This guide breaks down what each product does, who it’s built for, and how to choose between them.

What Is Binance Intelligence?

Binance Intelligence is Binance's lineup of three AI products: Binance AI, Binance AI Pro, and Agent OS. Rather than one tool trying to be everything, we’ve given you the ability to pick and choose what suits you best.

  • Binance AI sits inside the app as a 24/7 personal assistant. 

  • Binance AI Pro is a workbench for turning trading ideas into tested, automated workflows.

  • Agent OS gives developers a toolkit to connect their AI agents to Binance trading, market data, wallet, and payment capabilities.

See Which One Fits You

What Is Binance AI?

Binance AI is a personal assistant built into the Binance app that surfaces market context around the assets you hold and the way you use the app. The initial release leans on a handful of features: 

  • Generative UI reshapes the Markets Tab around whatever asset or event you’re looking at, pulling in summaries and analysis from trusted data that are personalized according to your usage and asset holdings. 

  • Market Brief gives a short read on crypto and traditional markets through the day, to read or listen to. 

  • Smart Tool Tips deliver contextual guidance based on where you are in the app and your experience level.

  • Master Trade shows how popular investors are positioned while leaving the decision to invest with you.

Note that Binance AI does not trade for you. It only arranges information around your situation so you can make better informed decisions.

How Does Binance AI Pro Work?

Binance AI Pro lets you describe a trading strategy in plain language, test it in practice mode, and run it as an automated workflow once you approve it, all without writing code. 

Some examples include:

  • Daily market report

  • Dollar-cost averaging plan for Bitcoin

  • Conservative approach for a $1,000 account

With your prompt written out, AI Pro will help plan out your strategy, fill in the gaps, and visualize the logic on a canvas. You can run the strategy in paper trading mode before any real money is involved. Going live needs your explicit approval and a functionality check from Binance AI Pro. 

The functionality check is only a confirmation that the logic executes without error. It is not a verdict on whether your strategy will make money. Each live workflow then runs in its own sub-account, walled off from your main balance. You can pause, adjust, or revoke your workflows from the app at any time. 

AI Pro is available on a free Standard plan that covers the whole path from idea to live trading, using DeepSeek and a monthly 250,000 credit allowance. The Premium plan at 19.99 USDC per month offers a monthly 10,000,000 credit allowance, manual top-ups, and access to frontier models such as ChatGPT and Claude, where available.

What Is Agent OS?

Agent OS is a developer platform that connects external AI agents to Binance capabilities such as trading, market data, wallet, and payments, within user-defined limits. 

The quickest way to connect is through the Binance MCP server. This allows your agent to read market data and trade on your behalf. Other capabilities, such as payments and on-chain activity, require other integrations within the Agent OS toolkit.

For security reasons, all agent permissions are turned off by default except the ability to read the user’s portfolio, balances, transaction history, and market data. Agent OS works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and ChatGPT, as well as self-built agents, and a Skills Hub supplies a curated library of skills so you don’t need to build from scratch.

Agent OS is not an autonomous trading system; an agent can only act on what you allow it to do. Like Binance AI Pro, agents use isolated sub-accounts separate from your main balance.

Which Binance Intelligence Product Should You Use?

If you want to keep making every call while the app explains more, stick to Binance AI. If you’re trying to build an automated trading workflow, try using AI Pro. If you’re building a full-on agent that acts within set limits, consider Agent OS.

Note that you don’t have to limit yourself to one of the three products. You might use Binance AI for a daily read of the market, while an AI Pro workflow handles your strategy in the background.

Final Thoughts

Binance Intelligence puts institutional-grade artificial intelligence in your hands, across crypto, stocks, and tokenized securities. Binance AI explains, AI Pro builds and runs what you approve, and Agent OS opens the door to agents with your permission. Whichever one you pick, you’re always in control. Our suite of AI products can only do as much as you permit them to.

If you’re still not sure where to start, Binance AI is the easiest on-ramp: no setup, no sub-account, just better context on what you already hold. From there, AI Pro and Agent OS are there whenever you’re ready to go further. For a long time, tools like this sat behind trading desks and research teams, reserved for people with the budget and the expertise to use them. Binance Intelligence puts that same caliber of tooling in your hands, and leaves every decision in them too.

Understanding What Binance Is (And Isn’t) Is the Best Defense Against Scams

2026-10-20

Main Takeaways

  • Understanding the true role of Binance and practicing critical thinking are essential defenses against increasingly sophisticated scams and impersonators.

  • Binance empowers users with tools and education for financial freedom but will never provide investment advice or solicit funds.

  • In an age of advanced AI and deepfake technology, maintaining skepticism and verifying information through official channels are crucial for staying safe.

Scammers have grown unnervingly good at pretending to be us. One of the most troubling tactics we see is the deepfake: lifelike, AI-generated impersonations of Binance executives and employees soliciting money on video calls that look and sound real enough to make anyone hesitate. The personas are fabricated, but the sophistication is genuine.

Every day, people are contacted by impersonators using the names, likenesses, and even job titles of Binance staff to solicit investments or financial transactions via WhatsApp, Telegram, and other channels. It’s devastating to see people scammed out of their money, and we feel a deep responsibility to address this directly.

We always try to warn and educate our users that neither Binance nor anyone representing it will ever contact you to offer investment advice or solicit funds. But with fakes becoming so realistic, we understand the fear and confusion many feel. How can we protect ourselves in an age where the truth is so easily manipulated?

One critical defense is understanding what Binance is and isn’t, and practicing critical thinking when interacting online. This clarity can help you recognize a scam the moment it asks you to act.

Is Binance a Financial Advisor? What Binance Does and Doesn’t Do

Binance is not a financial advisor, and it will never tell you where to invest or ask you for funds. A major source of confusion is a fundamental misunderstanding of what Binance stands for. As a global financial platform, Binance has become a household name for millions, synonymous with cryptocurrency, and even broader financial opportunity. 

For some, especially those new to financial services, the perception is that Binance is a one-stop solution for all things finance: a platform, a trusted financial advisor, and even a personal guide to managing money.

But here's the truth.

Binance is committed to empowering users by building the infrastructure for the future of finance. Our mission is to increase financial freedom by providing the tools and resources to explore digital assets and traditional finance in one place. We want to make it easy for you to start your financial journey and protect your funds, while equipping you with the education to make smart, informed decisions.

However, it's important to be crystal clear: Binance is not your financial advisor. We will never tell you where to invest your money, promise guaranteed returns, or ask you for funds. Our approach is all about empowerment: we teach you how to navigate the space, make your own choices, and take control of your financial future.

This principle is at the heart of everything we do, from our leadership team down to the customer support agents who are here to help you with questions. We believe in providing the best tools and resources, but the responsibility for financial decisions lies with you.

Binance is here to support your journey, not make the choices for you. Our platform is your gateway to financial exploration, but ultimately, the power to make decisions rests with you.

How Scammers Use AI and Deepfakes to Impersonate Binance Staff

This brings us back to the danger posed by skilled impersonators. Scammers prey on people's growing interest in investing and digital finance, and the trust they have in Binance, often masquerading as Binance employees or executives to exploit the credibility we've built. With advances in AI and deepfake technology, they can create personas that look and sound real.

Technology alone isn’t what makes these scams work. Scammers succeed by exploiting confusion and misplaced trust. They count on you to believe that Binance employees might contact you with unsolicited advice or "special opportunities." This is why it's vital to remember: no one from Binance will ever tell you how to spend your money or promise you returns.

If you ever receive such a message, pause and ask yourself: Is this person empowering me with knowledge, or are they directing me to act in a specific way? Does this feel like the behavior of a helpful guide, or someone trying to exploit my trust?

When in doubt, reach out to Binance through our official support channels. We're here to help you navigate the future of finance safely, but we rely on you to exercise caution and skepticism when approached online.

How to Protect Yourself From Online Scams

One of the best ways to protect yourself is to cultivate a healthy skepticism toward anything you come across online. Just because something seems convincing doesn't mean it's trustworthy. Technology can fake appearances, but it can't replicate the integrity behind a trusted platform like Binance.

Think of Binance as your compass, not your map. We equip you with the direction and tools to explore the world of finance, but the journey is yours to own. Scammers, on the other hand, are like fake maps – promising shortcuts to success, but leading you straight into traps that result in financial loss.

As AI technology continues to evolve, distinguishing between what's real and what's fake will only get harder. That’s why it's essential to stay grounded in what you know about Binance. Know what we stand for and, just as importantly, what we don’t do. We will never promise you easy profits or solicit funds. Keep these principles in mind, and you'll be better able to spot the difference between real opportunities and dangerous scams.

At Binance, we deeply empathize with those affected by scams. We understand the gravity of losing money to bad actors and the emotional toll it takes. That’s why we're committed to educating our users and ensuring they have the tools to protect themselves.

Remember this: Binance is here to empower you, not direct you.

In an era where seeing is no longer believing, let's rely on knowledge, principles, and critical thinking to guide us. Think of it as building a firewall in your mind – one that makes you much harder to fool. Stay safe, stay informed, and remember: the power to protect yourself lies with you.

The Rise of Programmable RWAs: From Tokenized Assets to On-Chain Utility

2026-10-16

Main Takeaways

  • Programmable RWAs are tokenized, on-chain real-world assets that can be lent, pooled and used as collateral.

  • On-chain RWA value is up 85.2% this year to $34.18B, but that’s still only about 0.01% of the markets it could reach. Past performance is not indicative of future results.

  • Binance Wallet is a self-custodial Web3 product, separate from Binance’s regulated exchange services, and one of many ways to explore programmable RWAs yourself.

*Note: Products and services mentioned here may not be available in your region. 

This article covers two separate things: research published by Binance Research, and information about Binance Wallet, a self-custodial Web3 product that gives users access to third-party Web3 protocols. Binance Wallet is not part of Binance's regulated exchange services. Using Binance Wallet is a separate choice from reading the research in this article.

RWA growth is broadening across major asset classes: bond and money-market funds drove 54.7% of this year’s on-chain AUM increase; equities another 22.4%. The more consequential shift lies in what happens once these assets are on-chain: whether they can be lent, pooled, or posted as collateral – that is, whether they are programmable. This blog examines what programmable RWAs are, the scale of their rise, and how to access them.

What are Programmable RWAs?

Programmable RWAs are real-world assets that have been tokenized and brought on-chain, with logic baked directly into their smart contracts. Rather than just representing an asset, they can enforce rules, automate payments, and serve as collateral or liquidity in on-chain markets. 

Explosive Growth, Room for Greater Penetration

Programmable RWAs are growing fast, and it’s still early days. One way to see how early is measuring Programmable Asset Ratio (PAR): the value of programmable on-chain assets as a share of the total market they could one day reach.

According to Binance Research, the markets tokenization could reach are worth more than $300 trillion. Just over $34 billion of that is on-chain today, a PAR of roughly 0.01%, which signals the market is growing quickly, and still has almost all of its potential ahead of it.

Equities and Bonds Lead the Way

Equities mirror this trend. Tokenized equities grew 390.4% this year to $4.43B, which is still only 0.0029% of the $151.9 trillion global listed-equity market. Meanwhile, their share of on-chain RWA value more than doubled from 4.9% to 13.0%.

Bonds and money-market funds are growing from a larger base. They hold $18.29B on-chain, with a PAR of about 0.0171%. That large pool of interest-bearing assets gives on-chain applications plenty to build on, while equities grow faster through wider distribution and easier access.

Room to Put Capital to Work

Utilization has plenty of room to grow too. Overall capital activation rate (CAR) is about 12%, so roughly $12 of every $100 in tokenized value is already being used in on-chain markets. The momentum is clear: equity CAR rose from 1.95% to 7.54% this year, and private credit has reached 49.67%. 

With so much tokenized capital still available to use, activation can keep growing without any new issuance. That makes the next opportunity twofold: bringing more assets on-chain, and giving holders more ways to use them across liquidity, lending and collateral markets.

A Separate Product: Binance Wallet

The research above comes from Binance Research and describes the broader programmable RWA market, independent of any specific Binance product. One option some users choose to explore programmable RWAs is Binance Wallet. 

Binance Wallet is a self-custodial Web3 product that gives users access to third-party Web3 protocols through its interface. It is operated separately from Binance's centralized exchange (CEX) and is not covered by the same regulatory status. You are solely responsible for your own custody, security, and compliance when using it.

How to Access Programmable RWAs

Binance Wallet gives you access to third-party protocols and dApps through its interface, but it is not the primary service provider for them, those services are operated independently.

1. Set up your Binance Wallet: The Binance Wallet is built into the Binance App. 

Open the app, go to [Wallet] > [Web3 Wallet] and tap [Create Wallet]. If you already have a wallet, you can import it instead.

2. Fund your wallet with a stablecoin: Stablecoins such as USDT and USDC hold a steady value and work with most token swaps, so they're a convenient starting point. 

Tap Receive in your wallet, then withdraw funds from your Binance Exchange account to your Binance Wallet, or fund it from another wallet address or with a credit or debit card. 

When the withdrawal or transfer is done, your stablecoin will show up under Assets. Note: You may need a gas token to perform the swap. Fund your wallet with a gas token the same way.

3. Open Binance Wallet’s trade tab: Use the wallet’s trade tab to access programmable RWAs such as tokenized stocks, ETFs, or other structured products.

4. Swap your stablecoin for a programmable RWA: Go to the Trade tab. Pick your preferred stablecoin to swap, enter how much of the programmable RWA you want to buy, and tap Approve & Swap. 

5. Store or use your programmable RWAs: Your tokens are now in your Binance Wallet, where you can hold them or use them on-chain.

Final Thoughts

Programmable RWAs turn tokenized real-world assets into ones you can use on-chain. With only about 0.01% of the markets they could reach tokenized so far, and about 12% of that capital already in use, there's plenty of room to grow. The shift from issuing assets to putting them to work is still in its early stages, and it’s one worth watching.

The next phase of growth likely depends on two things moving together: more assets coming on-chain, and more ways for holders to actually use what they already have. Equities and bonds are growing from different starting points, but both show the same pattern, low penetration, rising activation. That combination, rather than either number alone, is what signals where programmable RWAs go from here.

2026-10-15

Main Takeaways

  • Binance Academy’s new, free course, Understanding Bonds: From Lending to Fixed Income, explains how bonds work.

  • The course also covers how coupons, maturity, and yield work, why bond prices move inversely to interest rates, what credit ratings signal, and how bonds may fit into a balanced portfolio.

  • You don’t need any investing or finance background, and the course takes about 25-30 minutes across six modules in three sections.

The bond market is worth more than $100 trillion and sits at the center of global finance. Its core ideas of lending, interest and risk appear in every market, including crypto. But for many newcomers, the jargon alone (such as face value, coupon, yield, maturity) is enough to put them off. Binance Academy’s new free course, Understanding Bonds: From Lending to Fixed Income, cuts through that jargon and explains how bonds actually work.

Do You Need Prior Experience?

This course is designed with beginners in mind. Concepts are explained in plain language and build on each other step by step, focusing on ideas rather than the rules of any one country or platform, so it applies broadly. If you've already taken our Understanding Stocks: From Shares to Markets course, some ideas here may feel familiar.

Crypto users who already trade but have never studied traditional fixed-income markets may find it especially useful for connecting the two worlds. Interest rate expectations affect how willing people are to hold riskier assets, so the forces that move bonds can also shape crypto market sentiment. The mechanisms differ, but the lesson is the same: the price of money matters everywhere.

What You Will Learn

The course is divided into three sections and includes six modules. Each module is approximately four to five minutes, with a total course duration of around 25 to 30 minutes. By the end of the course, you'll be able to:

Understand What a Bond Is

A bond is a loan, and when you buy one, you’re the lender. The borrower owes you interest and has to pay back the full amount later. You'll learn the three basic terms every bond has: the amount borrowed (face value), the interest payments (coupon), and the repayment date (maturity). You'll also learn how owning a bond differs from owning stock. If a company runs into trouble, bondholders usually get paid before shareholders, but there's no direct upside when the company grows.

Learn Why Bonds Are Issued

Find out why governments and companies borrow by selling bonds instead of taking out bank loans or selling shares. You'll compare government and corporate bonds and see what the money pays for, such as roads, factories, or older debts. You'll also look at the key trade-offs. Borrowing has to be paid back with interest, but the owners keep full ownership. Selling shares brings in money with no repayment required, since investors receive a stake in the company instead.

Better Understand Coupons, Maturity, and Yield

Learn how a bond pays you and clear up one of the most common mix-ups in investing: coupon versus yield. The coupon is the fixed interest set when the bond is first sold. Maturity is the date you get your original money back. Yield is your actual return, based on the price you paid. If you pay less for the same interest payments, your return goes up.

Learn How Bond Prices and Risks Work

Explore the relationship between bond prices and interest rates. A simple seesaw example shows why an older bond paying 5% loses value once new bonds pay 7%. You'll also learn about the main types of bonds, including government, corporate, and high-yield bonds. You'll find out what credit ratings mean, understand the three real risks bonds carry (interest rate, credit, and inflation), and see how bonds can fit in a diversified portfolio.

Final Thoughts

While bonds aren’t crypto-native assets, the ideas behind them, such as lending, interest and risk, shape every market, crypto included. Real understanding comes from a clear picture of what a bond is, how the bond market behaves and where the risks lie. That's exactly what Understanding Bonds: From Lending to Fixed Income is built to cover.

Crypto, Stocks, and ETFs on Binance

For the last nine years, Binance has been building toward a financial system that’s more efficient, more accessible, and with fewer barriers. A core part of that vision has been creating a platform where users have greater command over their financial lives.

Over 7,000 U.S. stocks and ETFs now sit alongside crypto within one Binance app and account. Stock trading is available on an extended 24/5 schedule, because everyone should have the ability to react to market-moving news as they happen.

Alongside direct stock trading, we also launched bStocks, a tokenized securities product offering on-chain access to select U.S. stocks. With bStocks, users can trade their positions 24/7, take them off platform into their own wallets, and deploy them into DApps.

Direct stock trading and bStocks play an integral role in our super app vision, bringing crypto, equities, and on-chain finance into a unified user experience. For more details on bStocks, you can read our full announcement post.

The concept of diversified investing continues to expand, spanning across multiple asset classes. Today’s investors hold crypto, equities, ETFs, and stablecoins, and they want flexibility to move between them.

On Binance, the multi-asset experience has been simplified to a few taps. Users can go from Bitcoin to widely followed U.S. equities without switching platforms.

Reducing friction also goes beyond menus and interfaces. Billions of people have a phone and an internet connection, but limited access to traditional bank infrastructure. Because stock trades settle in stablecoins on Binance, even people who previously lacked access can now trade U.S. stocks on crypto-native rails. In the first week alone, over 80% of direct stock trading volume on Binance came from emerging-market users, showing how quickly demand surfaces when friction is reduced.

Stock trading on Binance marks the first time when people from eligible jurisdictions around the world can buy and sell U.S. stocks using stablecoins in a regulated manner.

Final Thoughts

Binance started with crypto, and crypto will remain our foundation. It is still the most open, programmable, and global financial rail available today. Everything we build is guided by our core mission of advancing equitable financial access and building a more transparent and safe system for all.

Bringing stocks and ETFs into the Binance ecosystem reflects what we’ve been doing since the beginning: give users the tools they need to control their own financial futures, whether it’s through 24/5 access to stablecoin-denominated U.S. stock trading pairs or the flexibility to trade across multiple asset classes on one simple interface trusted by over 300 million users.
